correctness.rationale: The state space has a bijective partial-permutation representation. Every legal edge slide corresponds to swapping the pivot and one permutation argument, with two legal hole placements. The potential n-c(pi)+2q_H(pi)+2epsilon changes by exactly one in absolute value on every edge, proving a lower bound. A complete four-case descent proves a path of equal length. Counting cycles and maximizing the potential yields the claimed diameter, and vertex transitivity gives the radius. Extracted Python verification exhaustively checks orders 2 through 8; independent edge-subset enumeration checks 2 through 5. Finite checks corroborate but are not the infinite proof.

Bousquet et al. (2018), arXiv:1812.05419, introduction lines 17-20 and Appendix B Lemma 5, explicitly use token jumping by default and prove jumping distances are k or k+1 for nonmaximal matchings; sliding is a stricter metric here.
Yamanaka et al. (2015) MIT repository abstract describes swapping distinct labelled tokens occupying graph vertices, not matchings of graph edges.

value.rationale: For a natural factorial-size matching state space the result gives the exact shortest sliding distance between every pair in O(n) cycle processing, a constructive optimal route and a parity-sensitive sharp linear diameter. It distinguishes constrained edge sliding from the known shorter jumping geodesics, and is not a routine matching count, a single table entry or an arbitrary parameter slice.
